model_answer:
## Bottom line

Netflix's global average monthly revenue per paying membership (ARM) rose from **$10.82 in 2019 to $11.70 in 2024** — an increase of **$0.88, or ~8% over five years (~1.6% CAGR)**. For comparison, streaming revenue nearly doubled (+96%, ~14.5%/yr) over the same span, driven overwhelmingly by member growth (+82% in average paying memberships), not by monetizing each member much more.

## The annual path (global, reported)

| Year | Avg. monthly revenue per paying membership | Avg. paying memberships | YoY ARM |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2019 | $10.82 | 152.98M | +5% |
| 2020 | $10.91 | 189.08M | +1% |
| 2021 | $11.67 | 210.78M | +7% |
| 2022 | $11.76 | 222.92M | +1% |
| 2023 | $11.64 | 240.89M | −1% |
| 2024 | $11.70 | 277.73M | +1% (4% constant currency) |

*Source: Netflix 10-K MD&A and regional streaming exhibits (FY2019–FY2024).*

Note the shape: essentially all of the five-year gain came in **2019–2022** (price increases in the US/UK/Europe, plus the 2022 launch of the ad tier and paid sharing). Since 2022 ARM has been roughly flat in reported dollars, because (a) cheaper ad-supported plans and lower-priced markets grew fastest, (b) the dollar strengthened sharply against EMEA/LATAM/APAC currencies in 2022–2024, and (c) Netflix cut prices in India.

## It's a very different story by region

| Region | 2019 ARM | 2024 ARM | 5-yr change |
|---|---|---|---|
| US & Canada | $12.57 | **$17.20** | **+37%** |
| EMEA | $10.33 | $10.96 | +6% |
| Latin America | $8.21 | $8.24 | ~flat (+21% in constant currency in 2024 alone) |
| Asia-Pacific | $9.24 | $7.29 | **−21%** |
| **Global** | **$10.82** | **$11.70** | **+8%** |

The US/Canada business — now ~45% of streaming revenue — is where pricing power actually showed up (six price increases in the period). Globally, ARM is being diluted by rapid subscriber growth in low-ARPU markets (India, Indonesia, Brazil) and by currency: APAC's reported ARM fell 5% in 2024 but only 3% in constant currency; LATAM fell 5% reported but *rose 21%* constant currency.

## Three caveats worth keeping in mind

1. **FX vs. real pricing.** In reported USD, ARM looks nearly stagnant since 2022; on a constant-currency basis, growth has been ~3–5%/yr each year. The 2022 10-K noted revenue would have been ~$1.77B higher at constant FX.
2. **Definitional creep.** ARM now includes advertising revenue (small but growing) and benefits from "extra member" sub-accounts, which generate revenue but are *not* counted in paid memberships — mechanically lifting revenue per counted member in 2023–24. It also excludes DVD by definition in all years.
3. **The metric is being retired.** Netflix stopped reporting quarterly memberships in 2024 and ceased disclosing memberships/ARM entirely in 2025, arguing engagement and revenue are better indicators — so FY2024 is the last clean ARM datapoint; from here, revenue growth has to be tracked through revenue and engagement disclosures.

**One-sentence answer:** Netflix's ARPU is up only ~8% in five years ($10.82 → $11.70/month), because price increases in the US/Canada (+37%) were largely offset by mix shift into low-ARPU Asia-Pacific and Latin America and by a strong dollar — member growth, not ARPU, has been the growth engine.
